figures.title: Chapter map
figures.why: three separations - horizontal from vertical, one frame from another, tangential from radial
figures.read: every result is a split into components, a frame subtraction, or a_c = v²/R

figures.title: The independence principle: two 1-D motions
figures.why: the chapter's single organising idea - split, solve each axis, rejoin at t
figures.data: x uniform, y accelerated at -g, shared t
figures.read: gravity acts vertically only; the axes never talk except through the clock

figures.title: The range formula: one question, two angles
figures.why: complementary angles are range twins and 45 degrees wins
figures.data: R = v0² sin2θ / g; R(θ)=R(90°-θ), max at 45°
figures.read: same range, different flight; 45° is the range champion

figures.title: Centripetal acceleration: turning uses no speed
figures.why: acceleration at constant speed, because the direction of v changes
figures.data: a_c = v²/R = ω²R = vω, toward the centre
figures.read: constant-speed circular motion is still accelerated, purely radially

figures.title: The safety parabola: reachable or not
figures.why: hit-or-miss problems for fixed speed reduce to one envelope curve
figures.data: envelope y = v0²/2g - g x²/2v0², vertex v0²/2g, intercept v0²/g
figures.read: a point is reachable exactly when it lies on or under the envelope

figures.title: Triage - route by the keyword
figures.why: the keyword names the route before any number is touched
figures.read: projectile words split axes, relative words subtract frames, circular words use v²/R

drawings.title: Horizontal motion and vertical fall
drawings.show: a ball launched horizontally from a cliff and a ball dropped vertically from the same height, shown at three equal time intervals. The dropped ball falls straight down; the launched ball falls the same vertical distance but also moves horizontally. At each time, both balls are at the same height — proving the vertical motions are identical.
drawings.search: "independence principle projectile horizontal drop same height diagram"

drawings.title: Oblique projectile motion
drawings.show: the parabolic trajectory of a projectile launched at angle $\theta$ with speed $v_0$ from the origin. $R$ (range) labelled on the $x$-axis; $H$ (maximum height) labelled on the $y$-axis; $T$ shown on a separate $t$-axis inset beneath the trajectory. The velocity vectors at launch, peak, and landing drawn: at launch ($v_0$ at angle $\theta$), at peak ($v_0\cos\theta$ horizontal), at landing ($v_0$ at angle $-\theta$). The symmetry of the parabola shown.
drawings.search: "oblique projectile trajectory range maximum height time of flight diagram"

drawings.title: Complementary projectile angles
drawings.show: two trajectories on the same axes: one at $\theta=30°$ (flatter, shorter flight time) and one at $\theta=60°$ (steeper, longer flight time). Both land at the same range $R$. The 45° trajectory (dashed) has the maximum range.
drawings.search: "projectile complementary angles same range 30 60 degrees diagram"

drawings.title: Projectile launched from a height
drawings.show: a projectile launched at angle $\theta$ from the edge of a cliff of height $h$. The trajectory extends beyond the cliff edge and hits the ground at a range $R$ beyond the cliff. The time of flight is longer than for ground-to-ground because the ball must fall the additional height $h$.
drawings.search: "projectile from cliff height h launch angle range diagram"

drawings.title: Rain and observer relative velocity
drawings.show: a man walking east (rightward) at $v_m$; rain falling vertically downward at $v_r$; the velocity of rain relative to the man drawn as a vector tilted from the vertical by angle $\alpha=\tan^{-1}(v_m/v_r)$. The man must tilt his umbrella forward (in the direction of the apparent rain).
drawings.search: "relative velocity rain man walking umbrella tilt angle diagram"

drawings.title: Angular velocity and tangential speed
drawings.show: a particle on a circle of radius $R$ at angle $\theta$; the arc length $s=R\theta$ traced out; the tangential velocity $v=R\omega$ drawn tangent to the circle; the angular velocity $\omega=d\theta/dt$ shown as the rate of sweeping out the angle.
drawings.search: "angular velocity tangential speed circle diagram omega R"

drawings.title: Geometric derivation of centripetal acceleration
drawings.show: a particle on a circle at two nearby positions, with velocity vectors $\mathbf{v}_1$ and $\mathbf{v}_2$ tangent to the circle. The change $\Delta\mathbf{v}=\mathbf{v}_2-\mathbf{v}_1$ is drawn, pointing toward the centre. The magnitude $|\Delta\mathbf{v}|=v\Delta\theta$ for small $\Delta\theta$. The acceleration $a=|\Delta\mathbf{v}|/\Delta t=v^2/R$ annotated.
drawings.search: "centripetal acceleration derivation geometric velocity change diagram"

drawings.title: Radial and tangential acceleration
drawings.show: a particle on a circle with velocity $v$ (tangent arrow); the centripetal acceleration $a_c=v^2/R$ (pointing inward); the tangential acceleration $a_t=dv/dt$ (tangent arrow, in the direction of increasing speed); the resultant $\mathbf{a}$ (diagonal arrow, tilted inward and forward).
drawings.search: "non-uniform circular motion tangential centripetal acceleration diagram"

drawings.title: Projectile on an inclined plane
drawings.show: an incline of angle $\alpha$ from the horizontal; a projectile launched at angle $\beta$ from the incline surface; the velocity components along and perpendicular to the incline shown; the parabolic trajectory in the vertical plane containing the launch direction and the incline; the range along the incline labelled.
drawings.search: "projectile on inclined plane angle from incline range diagram"

drawings.title: River crossing and ground-frame velocity
drawings.show: a river of width $d$ flowing at $v_r$ to the right; two boats starting from the left bank. Boat A points directly across (resultant path slanted downstream). Boat B points upstream at angle $\alpha$ (resultant path straight across). Both paths drawn as arrows; the drift of boat A and the crossing time of each annotated.
drawings.search: "river crossing boat drift straight across versus pointing upstream diagram"

drawings.title: Projectile safety parabola
drawings.show: several projectile trajectories for different launch angles (30°, 45°, 60°) from the same point with the same speed, all on the same axes. The envelope (safety parabola) drawn as a dashed curve touching all trajectories. The vertex of the envelope at height $v_0^2/(2g)$ and the far intercept at $R_{\max}=v_0^2/g$ annotated.
drawings.search: "safety parabola envelope projectile trajectories different angles diagram"

drawings.title: Acceleration vector in non-uniform circular motion
drawings.show: a particle on a circle with speed increasing (tangential acceleration $a_t$ forward); the centripetal acceleration $a_c$ pointing toward the centre; the resultant acceleration $\mathbf{a}$ tilted forward from the radial direction; the angle $\phi=\tan^{-1}(a_t/a_c)$ between $\mathbf{a}$ and the inward radial direction annotated.
drawings.search: "non-uniform circular motion total acceleration angle forward tilt"
